startersHint: A starter sets how the rows are put together. You can change every choice under More options after the table appears.
fileHint: Works on PDFs made on a computer, such as a bank statement, a marksheet or an invoice you downloaded. A photo or a scan has no text to read, so make it searchable first.
sampleNote: A made-up two-page bank statement, so you can see the result before using your own file.
noText: This PDF has no text that can be read. It is probably a scan or a photo. Use Scan to Searchable PDF first, then try again here.
failed: The PDF could not be read. Check that it opens normally and is not damaged.
tooLong: Only the first {max} pages were read.
noTable: No columns were found, so each line of the PDF is one row. If the PDF has a table, try the Marksheet or Invoice starter.
previewHint: The first rows are shown. Scroll sideways to see every column. Fix anything small in Excel after you save.
sheetsNote: Saved as {sheets} sheets, one for each page.
merge: Put all pages in one sheet
mergeHint: Switch off to keep each page on its own sheet.
dropHeaders: Remove the heading row that repeats on each page
joinWrapped: Join a line that wraps onto the next line
joinHint: A long description that continues on a second line becomes one cell.
skipHint: Leaves out the lines above the table, such as the bank name and account number.
numbersHint: So Excel can add them up. Phone numbers, account numbers and anything starting with 0 stay as text. Dates always stay as text.
outputHint: Both open in Excel, Google Sheets and Numbers. CSV has no sheets, so the pages are placed one after another.
notSaved: The PDF and the table stay on this device. Nothing is uploaded.
